instructions: Put the 1 1/4 cups oats, 2 tbsp flaxseed, 1/2 cup peanut butter, 1/3 cup honey, 1 tsp vanilla and 1/8 tsp salt in a large bowl. Add the chopped peanuts, 3 tbsp chocolate chips and 2 tbsp raisins.
Stir until everything is evenly coated. When you squeeze a little in your hand, it should hold together like a sticky dough.
Cover the bowl and put it in the fridge for 30 minutes, so it's firm enough to roll.
Scoop up a tablespoon of the mixture at a time and roll it between your palms into a 1 inch ball. This makes about 18 balls.
Eat them right away, or keep them in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 weeks. They also freeze for up to 3 months.
method_notes: Both stir rolled oats, peanut butter, honey and vanilla together with chocolate chips and a seed or nut add-in, then chill and roll the mixture into small balls that keep in the fridge. Well Plated (the lead) uses 1 1/4 cups oats to 1/2 cup nut butter and 1/3 cup honey, chills the bowl for 30 minutes before rolling, and its peanut butter version adds chocolate chips, chopped peanuts and raisins. Love and Lemons uses a full cup of peanut butter with ground flaxseed and coconut, rolls the balls first and then chills them for 1 to 2 hours. The flaxseed here fills the lead's 2 tbsp of 'power mix-ins', and its 1/4 tsp kosher salt is written as 1/8 tsp table salt.
